# FERB.app (notch UI, intro, sounds) (area `app`)

The Mac app the owner uses: notch, chat, settings, setup intro, orb, sounds, preview window, playground. The owner's side; talks to the daemon only through its RPC.

Active decisions here. Run `tools/kb/run kb show <file>` for the ones governing one file, their tests and open work; never reword an owner decision (supersede it).

- **APP-1** (owner): FERB.app's setup offers "Give FERB its own Google account (recommended)": the owner creates the account (creation needs human verification) and signs it into a browser profile; FERB finds and pairs it. If skipped, FERB browses as the owner in a profile the owner picks, and features that need FERB's own inbox say they aren't set up.
- **APP-2** (owner): FERB.app has, functional only (the owner polishes the UI later): Restore, listing FERB's Trash moves, backup copies and snapshots and restoring one; Delete, removing a stored owner secret or card; Uninstall, removing FERB fully, Keychain items included. Daemon RPCs plus minimal app screens.
- **APP-3** (owner): A button on each message in the notch opens the screenshot taken when it was sent and the images its task captured, each exactly as the model got it, with time and app or site. Settings → Data lists every saved screenshot of the last 7 days, newest first.
- **APP-4** (agent): FERB.app's how-tos, shortcuts and setting places are one list kept in NotchCore (AppGuide), beside the screens it names. FERB.app sends it with about.guide (APP_ONLY: only FERB.app's words become FERB's guide) on every connection; the daemon keeps it in memory and, until the app connects after a daemon start, the About document says so.
- **APP-5** (agent): FERB.app's Uninstall (plain or delete everything) awaits SMAppService.unregister() and checks the status; only not-registered or not-found goes on to `ferb uninstall [--purge --yes]`. A throw or a service macOS still lists shows why in the output lines and nothing is uninstalled.
- **APP-300** (owner): The notch shows the turn card with one row per part and its states (working spinner, done check, asks amber, couldn't-do red, updated tag, paused violet), the done/sites footer, questions with buttons inside a row, the plan-line bubble style and the typing-dots bubble; not the mock's dashed explanation labels or "code" chips. The UI work is functional; the owner polishes.
- **APP-301** (owner): When a part needs the owner (a question or a Yes) and when the whole task finishes, the notch opens itself without taking keyboard focus or switching apps. Rows that fill quietly only update the card. A macOS banner is the fallback only when the notch can't show (a full-screen app or video covers it, the display is asleep, FERB.app is quit); tapping it opens the notch.
- **APP-401** (agent): Setup has no separate hearing row: the microphone row covers Microphone and Speech Recognition (one grant for dictation and hearing); `ferb doctor` still probes hearing.
- **APP-402** (agent): Settings → General "Send dictation when I let go of the keys" (`voice.sendOnRelease`) is off by default. A sent draft that still holds the last dictated words goes with `speak: true`, so a dictated message lightly edited and sent with Return is still answered aloud; a typed message isn't.
- **APP-403** (owner): The notch shows a live picture of what FERB is working on: the task's own browser tab or the one Mac app window the current call targets, never the whole screen. The work-row circles, the popover and the floating player stream while a task runs.
- **APP-404** (owner): When FERB stops working in a window (moves to another step, pauses, waits, asks), the preview freezes on FERB's last frame of it and shows what FERB is doing now over it (asking, waiting, working in another app, paused). It never keeps streaming the owner's window after FERB has left it.
- **APP-405** (owner): There is no preview frame-rate cap until the heat is confirmed from data. Preview frames and capture time are counted (`resource_samples.work_json.preview`); step 13 measures the same task with the preview open vs closed, and the owner decides a cap from that.
- **APP-406** (owner): The preview popovers and the floating player are excluded from screen sharing and screen recordings (`sharingType = .none`).
- **APP-407** (agent): Every preview loop pauses while the displays sleep, the screen is locked or another user's session is in front (`PreviewAccess`); each video view asks only while its window is visible (occlusion); the work-row circles only while the notch is open and not stepped aside. The frame rate itself is unchanged (APP-405).
- **APP-500** (owner): First install is a short, interactive introduction that makes FERB feel like it belongs on the Mac: taught through small interactions, not slides, with the real notch central so setup feels like using the product; capable and warm, never cartoonish or theatrical. In one continuous tour a new user meets FERB, connects it, sees what it can do on their Mac, learns to control it and to bring it back, ending in the notch. The intro shows existing capabilities only; outside references are studied for principles, never their assets or flow.
- **APP-501** (owner): The notch is FERB's home and voice: it swells down to speak and shrinks back when done, and all of FERB's tour words come from it except a short instruction beside the orb. When FERB shows a place on screen, a small glass orb (an iridescent band inside that ripples while FERB listens or waits) drips off the notch in a liquid split, flies there, helps with the step, hops when the step is done, flies home and melts back; the notch swells once as it takes it back.
- **APP-502** (owner): In the tour FERB's lines are text in the notch, never read aloud; the only sound in the tour comes from FERB's sound family.
- **APP-503** (agent): While the orb helps with a step, a small frosted bubble next to it carries one instruction line (e.g. "Drag me into this list") and a reason line.
- **APP-504** (agent): Springs with a perceptual duration of about 0.35-0.5 s: opening with a small bounce (0.15-0.3), closing and dismissal critically damped (bounce 0), morphs snappy. Every animation is interruptible and retargetable mid-flight, keeping its velocity. Decorative animations last at most 2 s and the user never waits on one. Content stays concentric with the notch; the notch and the orb split and merge as liquid (metaball). Reduce Motion: springs become cross-fades and the orb fades in beside its target instead of flying.
- **APP-505** (owner): The tour runs: 1 Meet (the notch says hello in one or two lines; the full sound logo plays once); 2 Sign in; 3 Allow all, guided; 4 Pair all browsers; 5 FERB's own email, optional; 6 Try: look, tell, show the journey; 7 Control, taught by doing with today's controls (double-tap right Option, hold to talk, Control-Option-Space, stopping a task, pausing FERB), each done once; 8 Back to the notch: FERB small in the notch with one line on how to bring it back. Replay intro is in Settings.
- **APP-506** (agent): During Meet FERB installs its background service silently; if macOS asks for the Login Items approval (serviceNeedsApproval), the orb guides that one System Settings visit before sign-in.
- **APP-507** (agent): Sign in offers Codex or Claude first, with "Other ways to connect" for an Anthropic, OpenAI or Google API key. As soon as sign-in succeeds FERB starts the Mac scan (MEM-13) in the background so it is ready by the Try beat; a cancelled or failed sign-in never starts it.
- **APP-508** (owner): Every permission FERB asks at setup is required; setup grants them through one Allow all, and Automation stays per app at first use. Required grants still missing at the end bring setup back at the next launch.
- **APP-509** (agent): After an update a required grant counts as missing for FERB.app's own rows too (Notifications, Microphone), and the daemon's setup.finish checks every row before recording setup done.
- **APP-510** (owner): Allow all starts a guided sequence. For a list pane FERB opens the exact pane and the orb docks beside System Settings holding a real draggable FERB icon, follows the window and hides when Settings isn't in front; a request-style permission gets one notch line, then the system prompt. A grant counts only when the system confirms it, with a real check where the API can be stale, polled about every 1.5 s, never inferred from a drop. A grant that needs a restart restarts that part without losing the tour's place.
- **APP-511** (owner): The extension is added to every installed browser and one Pair all button pairs every profile at once; a per-profile Pair stays for those who want it. In the tour the orb flies to each browser's own "turn on" prompt if one appears.
- **APP-512** (owner): One beat offers FERB its own email for sign-ups and searches, now or later. Skipping costs nothing: it stays in Settings and FERB asks again the first time a task needs it.
- **APP-513** (owner): FERB says in one or two specific lines what it saw from the scan, then suggests two first tasks that fit this user, of different kinds where possible (one on the Mac or in files, one in the browser); with no clear scan, two general tasks. The user picks one and "Show the other one" previews the second. The preview shows the plan and the answer-in-steps rows and cards in the real chat UI, each marked as a preview, while the orb flies to the apps it would use. Nothing is clicked, typed, sent, opened or changed.
- **APP-514** (agent): A "Do it for real" choice taken in the Try beat starts as a normal real task, with its usual questions, only after the tour ends at Home. Stopping is practised in the Control beat on the Try beat's preview, replayed as a running preview.
- **APP-515** (agent): A resumed tour whose background service is down waits on "Getting my background part ready…" until the daemon answers or the owner skips.
- **APP-516** (owner): The tour can be skipped at any point, resumes at the same beat after a quit, and replays from Settings. A skip tears down everything the tour drew or said (orb, sound, drag card) at once and leaves the required steps still missing (service, sign-in, permissions) in the compact window. The app opts out of automatic termination during the tour.
- **APP-517** (owner): An install that finished setup never sees the tour (Settings offers Replay intro); one that finished setup but is missing grants gets only those beats plus Home. An install that never finished setup and predates the intro gets the full tour, as a first run.
- **APP-518** (owner): On a Mac without a hardware notch a virtual notch pill plays the notch's role, in the tour too: the orb launches from it on FERB's screen.
- **APP-519** (owner): The intro design fixes behaviour, flow, motion rules and the sound system; visual polish is the owner's, done in the Swift app. The look and feel is iterated in the intro playground, which runs the real intro code with everything behind it faked.
- **APP-520** (owner): FERB has an original, recognisable family of sounds sharing one character, each meaning one thing and recognisable without looking. A sound logo (full, tour only) seeds short derived cues, quieter and shorter the more often they play; needs you is the loudest everyday cue. Every sound has a visual twin, so FERB is fully understandable with sound off. FERB honours "Play user interface sound effects" and the alert volume, and never plays music under the tour.
- **APP-521** (owner): FERB makes a sound only for big events and where it is needed. Working is silent; there are no hover, typing or repeating progress sounds.
- **APP-522** (owner): In the tour sound is attached to FERB's position and movement, not a soundtrack: at the notch while FERB speaks, with the orb while it is out, home with it.
- **APP-523** (agent): Mono sources are placed from the notch's and the orb's frames: pan = clamp((x / screenWidth - 0.5) x 1.2, -0.6, 0.6), the notch at 0; distance from the notch lowers gain by at most 3 dB and adds a low-pass, never elevation or Doppler. HRTF (AVAudioEnvironmentNode) only when headphones are the output, equal-power pan otherwise. The engine stays warm and compensates output latency; no tight sync is promised on Bluetooth. Meaning never depends on position.
- **APP-524** (owner): The Crystal family, synthesised from code under the owner's direction with no samples, ships as FERB's own sounds; hiring a sound designer stays optional for later. No library loops or sample-library content, no game or film music.
- **APP-525** (owner): Google Material's "hero" clip (first launch) and "notification, high intensity" ship under CC BY 4.0 with their credit (Settings → About, Resources/Sounds/CREDITS.md, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, the app's ThirdPartyNotices.txt): the one exception to the family's own sounds.
- **APP-526** (owner): The tour and every everyday event play FERB's family through one engine, replacing the macOS system sounds. Every sound has its own switch: on by default for needs you, error, done, notification, listening start and end, and the tour; off for summon and paused. Standard is the default intensity, Subtle the choice in Settings. The master volume stays at 0.18; the existing master switch and volume carry over on upgrade.
- **APP-527** (owner): FERB has no magnetic docking sound; its setting is gone and an old value is cleared on upgrade.
- **APP-528** (owner): While another app is using the microphone (a call, dictation elsewhere), FERB plays no sound except needs you, at Subtle; the notch still shows everything. FERB's own dictation never counts as a call. Focus, quiet hours, screen sharing and media playing get no rule.
- **APP-529** (owner): As FERB first starts, Google Material's "hero" clip plays once; then no background sound until the notch plays the sound logo, which never starts before the clip ends. A replay or resume plays no clip.
- **APP-530** (owner): Bright Crystal glass plays the sound logo (Open fifth, tour only), summon, listening start and end, and done. Paused (one damped tap) and error (a sinking "uh-oh" onto a hollow B minor) use the same glass finger-damped: duller, an octave lower, no strike, so they never sound like completion.
- **APP-531** (owner): Needs you is "One ping": a single Crystal note on A (the unresolved dominant) left to ring; the loudest everyday cue.
- **APP-532** (owner): Material's "notification, high intensity" plays for every notification FERB gives: its macOS banners and the reminders, schedules and notices that arrive in the notch chat. A notice shown both as a banner and in the notch sounds once: the banner carries it and the notch stays silent for it.
- **APP-533** (agent): A banner carries the notification sound in the Standard mix (Subtle doesn't apply), at macOS's notification volume rather than FERB's. When macOS has FERB's notification sounds off, or a banner can't carry the sound, the banner posts silently and the app plays the sound. A wait on the owner (a question, a human check handed over) always sounds as needs you in the app, and its banner posts silently, so one event never sounds twice.
- **APP-534** (owner): The orb's drip-off (the old flight sound: one singing-glass swell, about 1.2 s) plays when it sets off, the hop when a step succeeds, the melt-back when it arrives at its target and when it comes home. There is no flight sound and no separate landing sound.
- **APP-535** (agent): One material, one 5-note pitch set, one room and one mastering chain; children change only contour, rhythm and length, cut down from the sound logo rather than composed anew. Frequent sounds vary a little per play (a few variants picked at random); the sound logo never varies. No loop while listening or working. Files are rendered offline by demo/sound-family/render.py (48 kHz/24-bit, Standard and Subtle, a room IR) and bundled losslessly as ALAC .caf; render.py is the source of every sound's level and length.
- **APP-536** (owner): The old FERB Voice helper (com.ferb.app) is merged into FERB.app: one app and one Speech Recognition grant, so the separate hearing permission row is gone and the microphone row (Microphone + Speech Recognition) covers hearing. Owner-facing text says FERB, never FERB Voice.
- **APP-537** (agent): FERB.app's executable answers transcribe, status and request-speech as FERB Voice did (same arguments, answer files, lease and exit codes). A hearing mode runs and exits before NSApplication, Sparkle, login items, the daemon connection or any window, with no microphone; an unknown first argument starts the normal app; a foreign FERB_HOME is refused first. Quitting before an update ends only the hearing instances FERB launched, by process id, never by bundle id, and spares a transcription in flight.
- **APP-550** (owner): FERB.app lives in the hardware notch: its idle footprint is native-sized and its hover surface compact.
- **APP-551** (owner): Panels use visibly frosted glass (blurred desktop, not plain transparency) with a pure black band extending below the camera and dissolving downward. Frost and black tint are one native background driven by the same display-link spring geometry as the controls: the blur mask never animates on its own, bare frost never shows before the tint and content, and SwiftUI opacity/clip groups never flatten the backdrop. Lower frost may be lighter. No white border lines around panels, buttons or fields; icons and real input fields over action labels.
- **APP-552** (owner): Double-tap right Option toggles FERB: it opens with focused typing when closed and closes when the dialog or pinned header is visible, with the same spring both ways. Voice opens at once while right Command + Option are held together (either Option key, either order); releasing either key finishes. Right Option alone never opens voice. Another modifier or an ordinary key cancels dictation and restores the previous draft. The previous app keeps its keyboard focus during held voice.
- **APP-553** (owner): Hover, double-tap, and returning by hover or click all focus the visible text input. Neither hover focus, typing nor ordinary controls pin the panel; only the explicit pin button keeps it across hover-out. Hover detection includes the exact physical top screen edge across the whole expanded header, wings included, with a 2-point vertical tolerance on the cutout and the expanded surface, so moving to the very top never dismisses.
- **APP-554** (owner): In the draft editor Return submits and Shift-Return inserts a newline, handled by the native NSTextView and preserving IME composition. No submission Tink and no unhandled-command beep.
- **APP-555** (owner): The header has a circular profile/options control and a pin toggle; no Preview label or ellipsis control. The centered "Go ahead. I’m here." greeting sits above the composer and the field placeholder is "Ask anything…". Voice is real dictation, never labelled microphone-off or simulated.
- **APP-556** (owner): The header pin is a 10.8-point regular glyph (10% under the original 12) in a 24 × 26 point click target. Profile is an explicitly sized 18 × 18 glyph in a 26 × 26 native button that opens an NSMenu. The header only fades; entrance scale and blur apply to the body alone. Neither opening nor lazy menu measurement resizes or shifts the profile glyph.
- **APP-557** (owner): Opening and hover exit share one 300 ms / 0.08-bounce spring; the exit follows a 60 ms grace period. Interruptions keep their velocity and the camera anchor stays fixed. Double-tap right Option opens with that spring and immediate text focus. Motion feels alive and continuous: persistent surfaces, interruption-safe springs, coherent transformations, responsive presses; Reduce Motion is respected.
- **APP-558** (owner): Pin keeps the header attached through hover-out, outside clicks, task submission and Space changes. Pinning or hovering away starts the upward tuck at once (no 1.5 s delay), with the shared spring and a fixed header. Hover reveals the body with focused typing and typing never folds it. Menus, file pickers and voice defer a requested fold until they finish; returning to hover cancels it. Hidden fields get no keyboard input. Escape, Hide or double-tap closes and clears the pin; Unpin returns to normal hover. Settings and Quick Look dismiss the unpinned notch.
- **APP-559** (owner): FERB's file picker, another process's menu, popover or floating window over FERB's drawn surface, or (pinned chat only) an app the owner brings forward or clicks into under the chat orders the panel out; when no reason remains it returns exactly as it was. Opening or revealing FERB, the notch, the shortcut and dictation keep it over windows overlapping it until they leave, so it is never stuck hidden. It never yields during dictation or to system text-input windows; always-on chrome (menu bar, status items, Dock, near-invisible or whole-display windows) never counts.
- **APP-560** (agent): FERB yields by ordering its windows out and back into the overlay space, never by toggling the panel's ignoresMouseEvents.
- **APP-561** (agent): The persistent content stack has an explicit, top-aligned presentation-height frame; its hidden full-height body never imposes a larger minimum height.
- **APP-562** (owner): Both overlay windows (the dialog and the trace) stay fixed to the physical notch during desktop swipes. FERB never moves or modifies other apps' windows or the owner's desktops. A Space change keeps the existing input responder: never resign key, reset geometry, restart the spring, discard state or seize focus FERB didn't already have. Background task updates never take focus from another app.
- **APP-563** (agent): The dialog and trace share one unmanaged SkyLight overlay space, above desktops and below security and lock screens. Private symbols are resolved defensively, both windows' membership is checked, and AppKit is the fallback when the space is unavailable.
- **APP-564** (owner): Work continues when the notch closes. Completion lights the camera edge with two soft green pulses separated by darkness (3.6 s total, a 1.8 s cadence), then off; Reduce Motion uses one quiet finite glow; it works hovered or closed and recalling a result never replays it. The dot in "ferb." shows status: amber while working, red for attention or error, green when done (kept by the session phase after the glow), neutral otherwise, with a tooltip and accessibility value. Hover shows compact status; Show activity reveals details.
- **APP-566** (owner): Sound feedback is a standing requirement. Submitting is silent (the owner rejected the Tink on Return); there are no hover or repeating progress sounds; right Option taps are silent, while the right Command + Option voice chord acknowledges at once. Mute and volume live in native Settings (Command-comma), and the system output volume and mute still apply.
- **APP-567** (owner): The owner does the visual evaluation and proposes changes; agents don't run unsolicited screenshot or UI inspection loops.
- **APP-568** (owner): FERB.app is connected to the real daemon. Dictation uses AVAudioEngine and Apple Speech with the system permission prompts, live transcription and review in the composer. Hold release, Stop, Cancel, hiding and switching to typing all stop capture; releasing while permissions are pending prevents a delayed recording.
- **APP-569** (owner): One continuous daily chat with no New request action. Approval secrets never enter chat history.
- **APP-570** (owner): Task events stream to the app as they arrive. Until the daemon emits reply deltas (it sends full answer text in reply and outcome), the app never claims token streaming works and never fakes it with delayed text.

- **APP-595** (agent): A launch after a grant restarted FERB reopens the setup step it restarted from, and Allow all asks for notifications without waiting on macOS's banner.

- **APP-598** (agent): While a grant waits on a switch that reaches the daemon only after a restart (Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Full Disk Access), FERB restarts its background service each time the owner leaves System Settings with the switch still reading off, never while a task runs. - **APP-599** (agent): When FERB.app installs or updates its service and macOS already lists it as enabled, FERB.app unregisters it first and then registers this build, so macOS records this build's launch constraint.
- **APP-600** (owner): FERB.app appears in the Dock (regular activation policy) while a titled FERB window is shown or minimized (setup, Settings, the preview player, What FERB saw), and is notch-only (accessory) when none is; the notch, the orb and other floating panels never count.
- **APP-601** (agent): At each launch of a packaged FERB.app, in the background, FERB removes com.apple.quarantine from every item inside its own bundle (links themselves, never their targets; the bundle folder last) and from nothing else. A translocated copy, a read-only volume (the disk image) or a bundle that carries none is left alone; any failure is quiet.
